The resulting step-size condition is τ<ζ(κ,D)−1/2, which recovers the Hilbert-space condition τ<1 as κ→0. Strong convergence to the point of Ω singled out, in the viscosity sense, by a contraction h:M→M is established, under an a priori bound D on the resolvent iterates and non-degeneracy of the self-adaptive step sizes. Numerical experiments on the manifold of symmetric positive definite matrices and on hyperbolic space accompany the theory.

Title: Vertically aligned large-area CVD-grown MoS2 nanoflake-based heterojunction for UV–Vis range photodetection: an electrical study
Author: Pallavi Gupta|Sandeep Chhoker
Abstract: This study presents an Al/n-MoS 2/ p-Si heterojunction photodetector, utilizing a large-area vertically aligned film synthesized via single-zone chemical vapor deposition. FE-SEM imaging confirms a uniform, vertically aligned flaky morphology with thin tip widths (10–20 nm), while Raman spectroscopy verifies highly coupled, crystalline multilayers. Electrical evaluations from 100 kHz to 1 MHz up to a 10 V bias assess charge transport under dark, UV, and visible illumination. The IV characteristics show predominantly ohmic contact at the metal-semiconductor interface, ensuring efficient carrier injection. Under light, the device exhibits enhanced conduction: conductance rises by 14.8% under UV and 2.8% under visible illumination compared to dark conditions. The superior UV response stems from higher-density photogenerated carriers and electron accumulation at the vertical flakes' sharp tips. Finally, frequency-dependent CV and GV measurements reveal interface trap states that influence carrier dynamics, highlighting this heterojunction’s strong promise for photodetection

Title: Can Chalcogenide Alloys Replace Traditional Photocatalysts for Sustainable Dye Degradation: Review
Author: Chandresh Kumari|Y. B. Saddeek|Kamal Abdel-Nabi Aly|Ishu Sharma|Pankaj Sharma|Sandeep Chhoker|Sunanda Sharda
Abstract: Water contamination by synthetic dyes, a pressing environmental and health concern, is primarily attributed to industrial wastewater discharge. Traditional dye removal methods, while effective, often suffer from high energy consumption and secondary pollution. Photocatalysis, a green and energy-efficient approach, offers a promising solution by completely mineralizing dyes into harmless byproducts. Chalcogenide alloys have emerged as innovative photocatalysts for dye degradation. Their narrow bandgap allows them to absorb a broader range of sunlight, while their cost-effectiveness and superior photocatalytic activity make them attractive for practical applications. This review delves into the potential of binary, ternary, and quaternary chalcogenide materials, examining their mechanisms of dye degradation, the impact of dopants, and their effectiveness in various wastewater treatment scenarios. Despite their advantages, chalcogenide alloys face specific challenges and limitations. Addressing these issues will be crucial for their widespread adoption in large-scale water treatment systems. This review concludes by identifying key research areas and proposing future directions to optimize the performance of chalcogenide-based photocatalysts for sustainable dye removal.

Title: Physics-based design and optimization of monolithic lead-free perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells with Cs 2 AgBiBr 6 as a high-performance top absorber
Author: Ajay Kumar|Nishant Dwivedi|Neha Gupta|Aditya Kumar Jain|Amit Kumar Goyal
Abstract: In this work, a comprehensive numerical simulation study of lead-free perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells was conducted using the SCAPS-1D simulation tool.

Title: Evaluating the Predictive Contribution of Receptor-Specific Docking Interactions to Aminergic GPCR Selectivity
Author: Vipul Kumar
Abstract: Molecular docking is often combined with ligand-based models to provide receptor-specific interaction information. In this study, we investigated whether such interactions improve the prediction of binding selectivity among aminergic G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) anti-targets using a stepwise approach. Native redocking successfully reproduced the crystallographic binding poses of the 5-HT2B, histamine H1, and muscarinic M2 receptors, but not those of the dopamine D2 and α1A-adrenergic receptors. In virtual screening against property-matched decoys, H1 and M2 showed moderate discrimination between active and decoy compounds, with ROC-AUC values of 0.717 and 0.704, respectively. In contrast, 5-HT2B performed near chance (ROC-AUC = 0.525), despite highly accurate pose reconstruction (RMSD = 0.14 Å). Structural comparison revealed only four identical ligand-contacting residues across the three receptors: Asp3x32, Ser3x36, Trp6x48, and Tyr7x42. We then examined 35 compounds with experimentally measured binding affinities at H1 and M2, comprising 19 promiscuous and 16 H1-selective compounds. The conserved Asp3x32 salt bridge was observed in 15/16 H1-selective and 12/19 promiscuous compounds docked to H1, compared with 3/16 and 5/19, respectively, at M2. Despite these differences in receptor–ligand interactions, incorporating docking-derived features into Morgan fingerprint-based classifiers did not consistently improve predictive performance under scaffold-grouped cross-validation. Compared with the ligand-only baseline (AUROC = 0.661), adding anchor interactions yielded a modest improvement (ΔAUROC = +0.020; 95% bootstrap interval: −0.029 to 0.088), whereas shell and extended-pocket contacts reduced performance (ΔAUROC = −0.062; 95% bootstrap interval: −0.154 to −0.010). The complete interaction fingerprint also provided no clear improvement (ΔAUROC = −0.029; 95% bootstrap interval: −0.118 to 0.036). Overall, these findings highlight that accurate pose reconstruction and structurally interpretable receptor–ligand interactions do not necessarily translate into improved ligand-based predictions of binding selectivity. Validation using larger datasets and independent receptor systems will be needed to determine whether docking-derived interactions provide predictive benefits beyond ligand-based descriptors.

Title: Active tunability of simultaneous electromagnetically induced transparency and reflection in a graphene-assisted planar terahertz metasurface
Author: Lavi Kumar Vaswani|Anuraj Panwar|Gagan Kumar
Abstract: We demonstrate actively tunable electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and electromagnetically induced reflection (EIR) in a planar coupled terahertz metasurface. The configuration comprises a cross resonator and two arc-shaped ring resonators placed in close proximity. The strong coupling between the resonators exhibits a transparency window in an otherwise absorptive region when placed in a near-field configuration. Passive tuning of the EIT and EIR responses is achieved by varying the resonator length, enabling precise control over the spectral characteristics of the coupled system. To achieve an actively tunable EIT and EIR effect, a monolayer of graphene is integrated to the metasurface, separated by a thin layer of flexible polyimide spacer. Variation in the Fermi energy of graphene results in active modulation of the EIT and EIR effects. A coupled oscillator theoretical model is employed to validate the simulation results and provide a deeper understanding of the coupling between the resonators. Furthermore, active modulation of the slow-light effect for both EIT and EIR effects is demonstrated. The study simultaneously demonstrates active EIT and EIR responses in the same metamaterial structure at resonance frequencies of 0.80 THz and 1.06 THz, respectively. This study also demonstrates the passive and active control of EIT and EIR effects, which can lead to the advancement of slow light devices, optical switches, and filters in the field of terahertz photonics.

Title: Cutting-edge trends in drought prediction and mitigation using ensemble learning and augmented XAI: a meteorological study
Author: Megha Rathi|Shailendra Mishra|Naif S. Alshammari|Himani Agrawal|Ehtesham Ashraf
Abstract: Drought affects more than 60% of India's population, reducing agricultural productivity, straining water resources, and threatening socioeconomic stability. This study proposes an interpretable one-month-ahead meteorological drought prediction framework by integrating class-weighted ensemble machine learning with SHAP and LIME explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Historical meteorological observations (1972–2022) obtained from the Zenodo climate database were analyzed for 49 districts across five drought-prone Indian states (Bihar, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka). After generating lagged meteorological features (t − 1 to t − 6) and addressing severe class imbalance (7.07% drought events), multiple machine learning classifiers were evaluated. The class-weighted XGBoost model (scale_pos_weight ≈ 11.90, without SMOTE) achieved the best overall performance on the independent 2016–2022 test dataset, with an accuracy of 95.7%, macro precision of 84.7%, macro recall of 81.0%, macro F1-score of 82.7%, and a PR-AUC of 0.647 on the highly imbalanced test set (outperforming both unweighted training and SMOTE-based approaches). SHAP and LIME consistently identified lagged Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), lagged precipitation, vapour pressure, and wet-day frequency as the most influential drivers of drought occurrence. Exploratory temporal analysis further revealed declining wet-day frequency in Karnataka, increasing vapour pressure in Andhra Pradesh, and substantial climatic variability across the study regions. The proposed framework combines accurate drought prediction with transparent model interpretation, providing a practical decision-support tool for district-level drought early warning, water resource management, and climate-resilient agricultural planning in India.

Title: A novel software clustering approach-based on large-scale many-objective optimization for object-oriented systems
Author: Amarjeet Prajapati|Anshu Parashar|Sunita Sunita|Alok Mishra
Abstract: Large-scale many-objective optimization problems (LSMaOPs) present a significant challenge for conventional evolutionary algorithms when trying to find optimal solutions. To overcome the limitations of conventional evolutionary algorithms in handling LSMaOPs, various improved algorithms, known as large-scale many-objective optimization algorithms (LSMaOAs), have been introduced. However, real-world LSMaOPs, particularly Large-Scale Many-Objective Software Clustering Problems (LSMaSCPs), demand more effective optimization approach. This paper introduces an Information Feedback Model (IFM) based LSMaOA called Large-scale Many-Objective Harmony Search (LSMaHS) designed to tackle the LSMaSCPs. To evaluate the performance of different variants of LSMaHS, they are tested on five different LSMaSCP instances and compared with existing LSMaOAs. The experimental results demonstrate that the variants LSMaHS-F1 and LSMaHS-R1 significantly outperform existing approaches, especially on more than 12 and 8 test problems out of 20 test problems, respectively. Thus, the proposed approach can assist software engineers more effectively in improving the maintainability and modularity of large applications.

Title: ARC-Trust+: Asynchronous Riemannian Coordination for Trust-Aware Decentralised Federated Intrusion Detection under Drift and Byzantine Attack
Author: Saumya Mishra|Shams Tahzib|Shailendra Mishra
Abstract: ARC-Trust+ is a fully decentralised framework for federated intrusion detection that combines a topology-aware exclusive neighbour cache with bounded staleness (TAEC), a Riemannian temporal deformation residual over symmetric positive-definite (SPD) covariance matrices (RTDR), a cryptographic canary consistency indicator (CCI), and composite trust evaluation (CTE) for trust-weighted aggregation and local isolation of Byzantine neighbours. This record archives the experimental notebook, requirements, results and figures accompanying the manuscript. The framework is evaluated on five public datasets (CSE-CIC-IDS2018, CIDDS, Edge-IIoTset, ToN-IoT and UNSW-NB15) under non-IID partitioning, five concept-drift regimes, and sign-flip, Gaussian-noise and ALIE attacks. Datasets are not redistributed; the notebook downloads them from their public sources.

Title: Impulse buying in online food delivery: A bibliometric and thematic analysis across three research domains
Author: Simran Seth|Garima Srivastav
Abstract: Online food delivery platforms have reshaped how consumers order food, and their design features may encourage unplanned, emotion driven purchases. Research on impulse buying and on online food delivery has each expanded considerably, yet the two streams have developed largely in isolation. This study maps their intersection using a bibliometric and thematic approach. Three Scopus corpora were built on impulse buying (n = 292), online food delivery (n = 1,251) and impulse buying in online food delivery (n = 77), giving 1,620 articles published between 2020 and 2025, with the intersection corpus extended to 2019. The screening followed a PRISMA protocol adapted for bibliometric work. Annual production, country output, source concentration (Bradford’s Law), keyword co-occurrence, thematic maps and country-level bibliographic coupling were analysed in R and Biblioshiny, while co-authorship networks were visualised in VOSviewer. Output grew in all three corpora until 2024, led by China, India and the United States, and the intersection corpus remained the smallest. British Food Journal and Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services appeared as leading outlets in more than one corpus. Key themes included customer satisfaction, trust, technology acceptance, the pandemic and live streaming, with only weak links between the two fields and little research from Africa, the Middle East and Latin America. The study identifies theoretical, contextual and cross-cultural gaps and proposes research questions on platform affordances, social presence and cultural moderators.

Title: STOML2: The Undercover Driver of Tumour Progression and Chemoresistance
Author: Vidushi Srivastava|Indrakant Kumar Singh|Keshav K. Singh|Shalini Mani
Abstract: Chemoresistance remains a critical barrier to effective cancer therapy, significantly limiting clinical outcomes across diverse malignancies. Emerging evidence highlights the pivotal role of mitochondrial homeostasis governed by mitochondrial dynamics, biogenesis, and mitophagy in driving adaptive resistance mechanisms in cancer cells. Among the key regulators of these processes, Stomatin-like protein 2 (STOML2), a mitochondrial inner membrane protein, has gained increasing attention for its role in maintaining mitochondrial integrity and supporting tumor cell survival. Recent studies demonstrate that STOML2 modulates mitophagy through interactions with essential regulators such as PINK1 and PARL, thereby influencing the turnover of damaged mitochondria and promoting resistance to chemotherapeutic stress. In addition, STOML2 has been implicated in the activation of multiple pro-survival signaling pathways, including NF-κB, MAPK, and IL6/STAT3, further enhancing cancer cell proliferation, metabolic adaptability, and therapeutic evasion. Its involvement in mitochondrial biogenesis also enables cancer cells to meet elevated bioenergetic and biosynthetic demands, reinforcing its role in tumor progression. Notably, aberrant overexpression of STOML2 has been reported across various cancer types and is consistently associated with poor prognosis and reduced treatment responsiveness, underscoring its potential as both a prognostic biomarker and a therapeutic target. However, despite accumulating functional insights, the structural basis of STOML2 activity and its precise mechanistic contributions to mitochondrial quality control remain insufficiently characterized, limiting its translational exploitation. By integrating molecular, cellular, and translational perspectives, this work aims to provide a comprehensive framework for advancing STOML2-focused interventions in cancer therapy.

Title: Diffusion of chiral active Brownian particles in oscillatory Poiseuille flow
Author: Anshika Sharma|Vikas Sharma|Narender Khatri|Suneet Kumar Awasthi
Abstract: Micro- and nanoswimmers diffusing in a fluid flow confined to microchannels are often described by overdamped active Brownian particle dynamics, in which viscous effects dominate and inertia is negligible. Here, we investigate the diffusive behavior of chiral self-propelled particles in a two-dimensional microchannel with oscillatory Poiseuille flow. Using numerical simulations, we show that the effective diffusion coefficient strongly depends on the oscillation frequency, flow strength, intrinsic angular velocity, and rotational diffusion rate. Interestingly, the effective diffusion coefficient can oscillate with oscillation frequency and flow strength, exhibiting distinct maxima and minima. The enhanced diffusion peaks arise from resonant diffusion associated with the matching between the flow oscillation time scale and the intrinsic characteristic diffusion time scale. Moreover, we identify an additional vorticity matching mechanism, leading to alternating channel wall accumulation of particles during successive flow half-cycles. Additionally, chiral particles strongly amplify the resonant diffusion, producing diffusion enhancements of several orders of magnitude compared to nonchiral particles. The results of this study could have implications for controlling the diffusion of self-propelled particles in microfluidic channels using time-dependent flow.

Title: From Algorithms to Empathy: Emotionally Intelligent AI Companions in Elder Mental Health Care - A scoping review
Author: Monika Sharma|Richa Chauhan
Abstract: Background: The rising mental health crisis among older people, which is caused by loneliness, cognitive loss, and a lack of emotional support, needs new and caring solutions. This systematic literature review looks at how emotional intelligence (EI) can be added to AI- powered virtual companions and how they can help improve mental health outcomes in elder healthcare services. Objective: The study’s goal is to find out how emotionally intelligent technology can improve traditional eldercare by delivering consistent, caring, customized emotional support by looking at existing applications and conceptual frameworks. Methods: A peer-reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2025 in the Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed databases. Studies that talked about emotional intelligence, virtual companions, mental health outcomes, or the design or implementation of eldercare services were included. A PRISMA-guided screening method chose 87 articles in all. The data was organized using the theme to identify common ideas and patterns in how virtual agents are used to help older people’s mental health. Results: The results show that there are five main themes: Emotional Responsiveness, Conceptual Frameworks, Psychological Outcomes, Usability and Acceptance, Ethical/System Integration, and Health System Integration. The results show that virtual companions with emotional intelligence may help older people feel less lonely, improve their mood, and make them more mentally strong. But the current collection of studies is not very complete; it has few real-world examples and no models that work across other cultures. Conclusion: This paper emphasizes the possibility of emotionally intelligent virtual companions as an aid in mental healthcare for the elderly. It underlines the critical demand for standardized conceptual frameworks, interdisciplinary research, and ethical principles to inform future breakthroughs and implementations. Emotionally intelligent AI technology could drastically transform aged care into a more responsive and person-centred service model in the digital era.

Title: Novel Electronically Controlled Current-Mode Design of a Grounded Capacitance Multiplier
Author: Atul Kumar|Bhartendu Chaturvedi
Abstract: This study introduces a current-mode grounded capacitance multiplier characterized by a straightforward design, electronic adjustability, and compatibility with CMOS technology. The circuit utilizes two operational transconductance amplifiers (OTAs), a current follower (CF), and a single passive capacitor, eliminating the need for matching components. The effective capacitance is electronically regulated with the help of OTA’s bias current. The operation of the active devices in subthreshold mode enables extremely low power consumption of 0.42 µW with a power supply of ±0.75 V. The suggested capacitance multiplier circuit can achieve a multiplication factor of 98.8 and a maximum deviation of 2.8%. The proposed circuit further demonstrates reliable performance across a broad frequency spectrum. Both ideal and non-ideal aspects are examined to assess real-world performance. The theoretical findings are validated through PSPICE simulations with 0.18 µm TSMC CMOS parameters. The proposed topology principle is also experimentally verified using commercially available ICs. The results obtained validate the proposed topology and demonstrate its appropriateness for real-world analog signal-processing applications.

Title: An AI-Based Minimax Optimization Approach for Cryptocurrency Price Prediction and Fraud Detection
Author: Tarun Mishra|Shivangi Saxena
Abstract: This paper explores the integration of AI (artificial intelligence) in predicting the volatility of the crypto space and detecting fraudulent activities by adopting the quantitative approach to examine fraud detection by using a CNN model and the ability to predict price volatility by using LSTM networks with the help of Google Colab. The findings of this study highlight that artificial intelligence is a critical enabler of long term stability and trust in the evolving crypto-space. The originality of this study lies in its investigation of the sustainable role of artificial intelligence in predicting future prices and detecting fraudulent activities simultaneously, and integrating efficiency, accuracy, and long-term applicability, which has been explored to a limited extent. Therefore, further research in other related sectors should be explored to understand the influence of artificial intelligence in Crypto-space. This study offers useful insights for regulators, policymakers, and portfolio managers and offers scope for further research. However, the study adopted secondary data for this research, which limits the research and its ability to capture the dynamic nature of cryptocurrency market.

Title: Hybrid bio-synthetic polymer gel electrolytes: Synergistic design and advanced applications for zinc-ion batteries
Author: Adnan Ahmed|Muhammad Ali|Nishant Yadav|Yinchun Fang|Xinhua Liu
Abstract: Zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) hold great promise for large-scale energy storage and wearable electronics owing to their high safety, raw material abundance, and environmental friendliness. However, conventional liquid electrolytes suffer from water decomposition, evaporation, and leakage, while zinc dendrites, anode corrosion, and hydrogen/oxygen evolution reactions further compromise battery stability. Polymer gel electrolytes mitigate these issues by forming hydrogen bonds with free water, yet gels based on a single biopolymer gel (BPG) or a single synthetic polymer gel (SPG) electrolytes show clear performance trade-offs, where BPGs offer biocompatibility and good interfacial regulation but lack mechanical strength and high ionic conductivity, whereas SPGs provide strong mechanical properties but poor biocompatibility and weak electrode modulation. This review examines emerging hybrid bio-synthetic gel (HB-SG) electrolytes that combine the strengths of both polymer systems, covering their design principles, four main structural types, key synergistic mechanisms, and fabrication methods. Their performance in ion transport, mechanical resilience, self-healing, temperature tolerance, and resistance to parasitic reactions is discussed alongside practical applications across flexible, extreme-environment, and harsh-condition ZIBs. Current challenges, unclear synergistic mechanisms, limited room-temperature ionic conductivity, storage instability, and industrial scalability barriers are identified, along with future directions including multiscale structural design, theoretical simulation, green manufacturing, intelligent functionalization, and biomedical applications.

Title: Environmental and Climate-Resilient Approaches to Scour Depth Prediction: From Empirical Equations to Advanced Machine Learning Models
Author: Amreen Khatun|Ashish Kumar|Neel Kanth|Parveen Berwal
Abstract: Scour around bridge structures is a major cause of bridge failure, disturbing sediments and aquatic habitats; therefore, accurate prediction for structural safety and river ecosystem protection is necessary. This study bridges the gap between research and practice by highlighting the disconnect between Machine Learning (ML)- based prediction and current conventional design methods, and systematically compares their performance using consistent statistical indicators. The analysis showed that dataset size ranged from 100 to 871 samples, with an inconsistent relationship between sample size and predictive accuracy (R² = 0.850–0.959), whereas a mid-sized dataset of 500 samples performed best (R² = 0.959), indicating that no single factor determines optimal model performance. Therefore, this study recommends applying large-scale field datasets alongside laboratory datasets in different machine learning models to achieve more precise and reliable results. Such advancements can reduce unnecessary streambed disturbance and improve prediction reliability, supporting more sustainable river infrastructure.

Title: Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants in India: plant-level features, model results and gas-grid siting scores
Author: Rajshree Singh
Abstract: Plant-level dataset of the 776 Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants registered on the GOBARdhan portal (Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, India; snapshot 22 October 2026). Each plant is joined with distance to the nearest gas-pipeline IP/SV with tap-off, residual CBG intake capacity of its city-gas geographical area, crop residue and cattle/buffalo dung within 20 km, nearby competing capacity, project design and developer markers. The package also contains cross-validated machine-learning results (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost) classifying operational versus not-yet-started plants, SHAP feature importance, robustness analyses, siting scores for 6,257 grid cells within 75 km of a tap-off, and a ranking of 701 tap-off points. Analysis code: https://github.com/rajshree-singh/cbg-siting-india

Title: When Algorithms Set Prices: Emerging Consumer Fairness Challenges in AI-Driven Dynamic Pricing
Author: Ashutosh Sharma|Suresh Sannapu
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is turning dynamic pricing from a standardized management decision into an individual, algorithmic experience. Algorithmic pricing improves efficiency and personalization, but its opacity and individualized prices can leave consumers feeling treated unfairly and distrustful. This short communication draws on recent research on algorithmic pricing, price fairness, price transparency, and consumer trust to build a conceptual framework. It links four features of algorithmic pricing (real-time adaptation, personalization, individualized price differentiation, and limited explainability) to perceived price fairness, which in turn shapes consumer trust and acceptance or resistance. The paper argues that fairness is a strategic management problem, not only an ethical concern. Implications for pricing managers cover price explanations, responsible personalization, and governance, and empirical research directions are proposed.

Title: Phase‐Engineered MoS 2 Photoelectrodes for Solar Hydrogen Production: Mechanistic Comparison of Semiconducting 2H and Metallic 1T Phases for Enhanced Charge Transfer and Catalytic Efficiency
Author: Himani Khyalia|Narinder Kaur
Abstract: Phase manipulation of transition metal dichalcogenides is presented as a promising approach for designing and tuning the electronic band structure and catalytic activity for solar‐driven hydrogen production. In this work, phase‐pure with a distinct electronic band semiconducting 2H‐MoS 2 and metallic 1T‐MoS 2 were synthesized through controlled hydrothermal technique. Significantly improved photocurrent density to 4.2 mA cm −2 at 1.0 V, donor density, lower charge‐transfer resistance, and improved incident photon‐to‐current efficiency of ∼30% were achieved for the 1T‐MoS 2 . Faradaic efficiency experiments demonstrated highly efficient hydrogen production ∼95% with stable operation over 4.2 h for 1T‐MoS 2 , while 2H‐MoS 2 showed lower catalytic activity with higher structural stability. These results suggest that enhanced charge‐transfer kinetics, higher carrier concentration, and phase‐associated structural disorder play a more significant role in determining photoelectrochemical(PEC) activity than optical absorption alone. This work provides insight into phase‐dependent catalytic activity of MoS 2 and demonstrates crystal phase engineering as a powerful tool for designing highly efficient photoelectrodes.

Title: Code for "Escaping AB caging via Floquet engineering: drive-induced long-range interference in an all-band-flat model"
Author: Aamna Ahmed|Mónica Benito|Beatriz Pérez-González
Abstract: Python code to reproduce all figures of A. Ahmed, M. Benito and B. Pérez-González, "Escaping AB caging via Floquet engineering: drive-induced long-range interference in an all-band-flat model", arXiv:2511.20255. The model is a π-flux diamond (rhombic) chain whose on-site energies are driven by a square wave. The code computes its exact Floquet spectrum and stroboscopic dynamics, the high-frequency effective Hamiltonian and its mapping to a decorated Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, Zak phases, and the dynamics and entanglement of two interacting fermions. Each figure has a Jupyter notebook that computes its data, and a separate notebook makes all the figures. The numerical data is not included; it is generated by running the notebooks. Dependencies are pinned with uv (Python 3.13). README.md explains how to install and run the code and maps each figure to its notebook, data file and figure file.

Title: Performance Analysis of a Finite Markovian Queue with Admission Control F-Policy with Service Interruptions and Vacations in Transient Mode
Author: Aayushi Gangwar|Amita Bhagat
Abstract: The present study investigates a finite-capacity single-server queueing model under admission control F-policy (ACFP). The system can accommodate a maximum of K number of customers, maintaining the quality of service for limited capacity. Moreover, the system has the provision of an admission F-policy that controls the outbreak of customers in the system after finite capacity has been achieved. The server is prone to random breakdowns and is sent for repair to resume normal services after repair. The server has the privilege to go for vacations, particularly working vacations, when no more customers are available for the service. During this state, the server continues to operate at a reduced service rate during which routine maintenance may also be performed. The queueing model under consideration is novel and versatile owing to realistic features involving ACFP, working vacations and maintenance states, referring to many realistic applications like hydro power plants, hospital diagnostic centres, etc. The queueing model is investigated in a transient state so as to study its performance and efficiency challenges with time. The transient equations are formulated using the Chapman-Kolmogorov approach, and analysis of the model has been carried out using the Runge-Kutta method. Various performance measures are obtained numerically to investigate the model under study in a data-driven manner. Moreover, the detailed application of the model for hospital diagnostic centres has also been discussed.

Title: Enhancing Solar Still Productivity through Fin, Solar Collector and Wick Modifications: A Comprehensive Review
Author: Akashdeep Negi|Lalit Ranakoti|Kapil Kumar Sharma|Adhirath Mandal|Mansi Sharma|Deepak Kumar|Jeetendra Mohan Khare|Shobhit Sharma|Prabhakar Bhandari|Sneha Singh
Abstract: Solar distillation has emerged as a vital technique for providing fresh water to communities at an economic level. Among various systems, the solar still has been recognised as a promising technology due to its simple design, low maintenance requirements and environmental benefits, particularly in reducing carbon footprint and supporting sustainable development goals. However, the yield of a solar still is highly dependent on solar intensity, which drops significantly at night, thereby limiting its overall efficiency. So, this review article explores a wide range of low-cost modifications for improving the evaporation rate and freshwater yield. The article covers the fabrication process of the solar still and discusses various design modifications. These modifications include the effects of fin geometry and placement. Furthermore, the article examines the integration of external attachments such as flat plate collectors (FPC) and evacuated tube collectors (ETC) to enhance heat transfer. The influence of wick materials, their types and placement within the solar still are also analysed. Lastly, the article provides a key recommendation highlighting the potential future research for the development of high-performance solar stills.

Title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF ANTIOXIDANT CAPACITY AND PHYTOCHEMICAL COMPOSITION IN PLANT AND ANIMAL BASED FOODS
Author: Rajesh Kumar1|Himanshu Saini|Umang Billoria3|Tina Sharma3|Anjana Sagar
Abstract: Antioxidants play a crucial role in reducing oxidative stress by neutralizing free radicals, thereby protecting cellular components and maintaining overall health. Dietary antioxidants are primarily obtained from plantbased foods. The present study aimed to comparatively evaluate the antioxidant capacity of selected plantbased (vegan) and animal- based (non-vegan) foods using the DPPH (2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl) radical scavenging assay. Quantitative assessment of antioxidant compounds was executed using a spectrophotometric method. Methanolic extracts of selected vegan foods, including fruit pulp of Syzygium cumini (jamun), whole gain of Pennisetum glaucum (bajra), seeds of Glycine max (soybean) and polished grain of Oryza sativa (rice), as well as non-vegan foods such as muscle tissue of Catla catla (fish), muscle tissue of Gallus gallus domesticus (chicken), whole milk and a milk-based probiotic drink, were prepared and analyzed. The DPPH assay demonstrated that Syzygium cumini depicted the highest radical scavenging activity with 95.54% inhibitionat 100 µL. Glycine max and Pennisetum glaucum also showed strong antioxidant potential, whereas rice displayed comparatively lower activity among the vegan samples. Among the nonvegan foods, chicken and fish exhibited moderate inhibition (approximately 77–88%), while milk and the probiotic drink showed relatively lower antioxidant activity. Overall, the results indicate that plant-based foods possess greater antioxidant diversity and stronger radical scavenging potential compared to the animal-derived foods examined. These findings underscore the nutritional importance of plant-based foods and demonstrate the effectiveness of spectrophotometric techniques for antioxidant screening, while highlighting the need for complementary assays to fully characterize antioxidant capacity.

Title: NeuroState: A Comparative Framework for Electroencephalography-Based Meditative State Classification
Author: Anirudh Pratap Singh|Manas Sharma|Aryan Raj|Vijay Khare
Abstract: Accurate identification of meditative states using electroencephalography (EEG) is crucial for objective neural assessment and brain-computer interface applications. However, reliable classification remains challenging because of signal nonstationarity, artifacts, inter-individual variability, and differences across recording sessions. To address these challenges, NeuroState, a dual-path classification framework integrating time-frequency analysis, conventional machine learning, and attention-enhanced deep learning, was developed for automated classification of meditation-related cognitive states. Initially, EEG signals were transformed into time-frequency representations using the Morlet continuous wavelet transform (CWT), allowing temporal variations in spectral activity to be characterized. Two complementary classification pathways were subsequently implemented. In the conventional machine-learning pathway, wavelet-derived scalograms were vectorized, and dimensionality was reduced using principal component analysis (PCA) before classification with support vector machine and random forest classifiers. In the deep-learning pathway, the two-dimensional scalograms were directly processed using a wide squeeze-and-excitation residual network, in which residual feature extraction and channel-wise attention were integrated to facilitate the adaptive learning of discriminative time-frequency representations. The framework was evaluated using the publicly available OpenNeuro ds001787 dataset, comprising EEG recordings from 24 participants, including 12 experienced meditators and 12 individuals with limited meditation experience. The wide squeeze-and-excitation residual network achieved a test accuracy of 98.29%, outperforming the support vector machine and random forest classifiers, which achieved accuracies of 88.59% and 81.65%, respectively. These findings demonstrate the superior classification performance of attention-enhanced deep learning compared with the evaluated conventional machine-learning approaches. These findings suggest that attention-enhanced deep learning applied to structured EEG time-frequency representations may provide more accurate discrimination of meditation-related cognitive states than conventional machine-learning approaches based on PCA-reduced features. NeuroState thus provides a promising computational framework for EEG-based meditative state classification, with potential applications in meditation monitoring, neurofeedback, and brain-computer interface systems.

Title: Fracture analysis of spacecraft cylindrical pressure vessels under combined pressure and temperature
Author: Richa Sharma|Anuj Bhardwaj|Anshu Nagar
Abstract: Cylindrical pressure vessels are integral structural components in modern spacecraft. They are used to hold propellants, coolant fluids, and life-support gases at high pressure in spacecrafts. Fracture analysis of these cylindrical pressure vessels is essential for assuring their structural durability under the effects of internal pressure and temperature. During orbital operations, these vessels are exposed to rapid temperature fluctuations caused by solar radiation and deep-space cooling, which generate substantial thermomechanical stresses. This study investigates the fracture behaviour of cylindrical pressure vessels subjected to combined pressure and thermal loading to support the development of more resilient spacecraft structures. The elastic-plastic stresses in a thick-walled cylinder composed of functionally graded isotropic material subjected to internal pressure and external temperature is obtained by using analytical method. By applying the boundary conditions, the governing differential equation is solved to determine the stresses. Based on graphs and mathematical computations, it is observed that if the value of temperature increases, stresses on inner surface increase, whereas decrease on the outer surface of the cylindrical pressure vessel. Also, stresses increase on the inner surface when pressure increases. Therefore, it can be concluded that thick-walled cylindrical pressure vessel of FGM (aluminium) is more suitable in direct sunlight (for extremely high temperatures), and the cylindrical pressure vessel of FGM (stainless steel) is more suitable under shadow (for extremely low temperatures) for crew and life support systems in spacecraft design.

Title: Re-description of Durinemella elongata Andrássy 2009, andUniqaxonchium megaspiculatum Dhanam & Jairajpuri 1998 (Nematoda: Belondiroidea) with emended generic diagnosis
Author: Sumit Kumar|Wasim Ahmad
Abstract: The population of Durinemella elongata and Uniqaxonchium megaspiculatum were isolated from the soil samples collected from Western Ghats of India. We compared our isolated specimens with the original description of both the species. The inconsistences in morphology, morphometrics, and some errors in the original description of these species encouraged us to re-describe them. The newly recorded specimen of Durinemella elongata showed a thin sheath surrounding the expanded part of the pharynx without spiral bands, which was not mentioned in original description. Additionally, we noted cheilostom with a weak basket-like structure in our specimens, instead of cuticularized refractive elements around oral aperture described originally. Other key characteristics include a cylindrical, tongue-like cardia with the intestine attached at its posterior tip, amphidelphic female genital system, slender and arcuate spicules, 3-4widely spaced ventromedian supplement, and a long, filiform whip-like tail. Uniqaxonchium megaspiculatum is also re-described with new morphological and morphometics data, along with SEM and LMphotographs. It is characterised by an offset lip region, a fusiformodontostyle, pharynx long with its posterior expanded part separated by a deep constriction from the anterior slender part; female genital system mono-opishthodelphic, vagina more than corresponding body diameter deep, highly inclined posteriad. Male with long slender, arcuate spicules, 4-7 ventromedian supplements, along with a short, hemispheroid tail, similar in sexes. Based on this new morphological and morphometrics data, we have emended the generic diagnosis for both the genera Durinemella and Uniqaxonchium, providing detailed description for their type species.

Title: Polynomial-Time Analytical Relaxation of the Travelling Salesman Problem via Probability-Flow Tensors and Maclaurin Series Expansions
Author: Udaysagar Kandpal
Abstract: The Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP) remains a canonical NP-hard combinatorial optimization challenge,traditionally bound by factorial O(N!) or exponential O(N² 2^N) computational complexities. This paperpresents a novel continuous-analytical framework that maps discrete permutation spaces onto a continuousprobability-flow tensor manifold. By reformulating edge transitions through stochastic matrices, cumulativeproduct normalization, transcendental scaling factors, and truncated Maclaurin series expansions of pathgenerating functions, we bypass exponential subset enumeration. We introduce a deterministic algorithmexecuting in strict O(N³) polynomial time, demonstrating empirical alignment with known optimal baselineswhile ensuring stable scalability for enterprise-scale graph topologies.

Title: Optical Solitons in a Cascaded Quadratic Medium by the Lie Symmetry Method and a Generalized G′/G-Expansion Approach
Author: Lakhveer Kaur|Mohamed E.M. Alngar|Houria Triki|Anjan Biswas
Abstract: Optical solitary waves in a cascaded quadratic medium are investigated using the Lie symmetry analysis and a generalized G′/G-expansion approach. The governing nonlinear evolution equation incorporates group-velocity dispersion, self-phase modulation, and two nonlinear derivative terms representing self-steepening contributions. Its real-valued formulation admits a four-dimensional non-Abelian symmetry algebra comprising phase rotation, translations, and a combined scaling and phase transformation. A traveling-wave reduction establishes compatibility conditions linking the wave velocity and self-steepening coefficients and yields a second-order nonlinear ordinary differential equation. The generalized expansion produces two parameter branches of exact hyperbolic wave solutions, including combo-bright-singular, dark, and singular structures subject to explicit parameter and denominator conditions. The analytical solution families are further examined through direct residual verification, linear spectral analysis, and modulation instability analysis, providing independent assessments of their validity and the stability of the nonzero background supporting the dark-soliton solution. For a representative admissible parameter set, the selected dark-soliton profile exhibits a localized intensity notch on a finite background and translates uniformly with the propagation coordinate. Three-dimensional surfaces, two-dimensional profiles, and contour plots of the intensity, modulus, and real and imaginary components distinguish envelope translation from carrier-phase evolution. The results provide a systematic characterization of the admissible solution branches, their regularity conditions, and their stability properties, while offering analytical reference profiles for subsequent numerical propagation and perturbation studies.

Title: NAVIGATING URBAN GROWTH IN THE HIMALAYAS: LULC SHIFTS AND SUSTAINABLE PLANNING IN SHIMLA FOR SUSTAINABLE MOUNTAIN ECOSYSTEMS AND URBAN GROWTH
Author: Akash Bhardwaj|Ashok Kumar Gupta
Abstract: Widespread anthropogenic alteration of the Earth's surface, especially in vulnerability-sensitive mountain landscapes defines the Anthropocene. This research examines the spatio-temporal dynamics of Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) in Shimla District, Himachal Pradesh, India, over the period 2017–2024, with analyses conducted for the years 2017, 2021, and 2024. The predictions are also calculated and analysed using CA-Markov forecast predicting the dynamics change for 2030 and 2035. High-resolution, multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery were considered for the study and analysed using ArcGIS. The supervised classification technique was used to classify the landscape into nine different land use land cover categories. Most strikingly, the results show a significant land expansion in built up area largely at the expense of important ecological buffers. In this time frame, tree cover experienced a loss of around 4%, surface water bodies declined by 25%, and agricultural croplands displayed sporadic but notable reductions of 33% in the same time period up until 2024. Extrapolating into the future, these changes indicate a substantial annualized rate of urban expansion based on the Puyravaud Annual Rate of Change method, which is not sustainable. The study predicts that, with no intervention, a CA-Markov forecast predicts built-up land to reach approximately 750 km² by 2035 will likely lead to additional reductions in both forest and agricultural reserves. The imbalance between development and environmental stability is associated with growing exposure to disasters such as by rainfall-triggered landslide happened in 2023 and 2025 accompanied by seasonal urban water stress. The article critically examines present-day urban policy trajectories and posits sustainable spatial planning as an inevitable mode of Himalayan urbanism for the future.

Title: Targeting Cancer Mitochondria with Stimuli-Responsive Nanocarriers: Emerging Strategies for Precision Oncology
Author: Kartik Bhatnagar|Geeta Swargiary|Sakshi Tyagi|Aditi Kaushik|Vaibhav Mani Tripathi|Keshav K. Singh|Shalini Mani
Abstract: Mitochondria are central regulators of cancer cell survival, metabolism, and therapy resistance, making them a promising yet underutilized target in modern oncology. Internal stimuli such as altered redox balance, elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS), and acidic pH uniquely characterize the tumor microenvironment, providing a distinct trigger for smart drug delivery. Internal stimuli-responsive nanocarriers have emerged as an innovative strategy to achieve spatiotemporal control of drug release while selectively homing to subcellular organelles such as mitochondria. This review outlines the multifaceted role of mitochondria in cancer progression, chemoresistance, and metastasis, and highlights the unique biochemical hallmarks of cancer cells that facilitate targeted delivery. We further explore recent advances in the development of pH-, redox-, ROS-, and enzyme-sensitive nanocarriers that exploit these internal cues to localize chemotherapeutic agents specifically to cancerous mitochondria. We also compare their advantages and limitations with conventional chemotherapy and other targeting approaches. Additionally, translational challenges, limitations, and future directions including vesicle-mediated mitochondria transfer are discussed, aiming to reduce systemic toxicity while improving therapeutic efficacy.

Title: Effect of Lanthanum Doping on Spray‐Deposited ZnO Thin Films for Carbon Monoxide Gas‐Sensing Applications
Author: Bhawna|Vinay Narwal|Rashmi Singh|Amanpal Singh|Dinesh Kumar|Ekta Yadav|Sanjay Kumar Swami|Anuj Kumar|Manoj Kumar
Abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) detection is crucial in several areas, such as environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and health care, due to its colorless, odorless, and highly toxic nature even at low concentrations. In this study, we report the effect of lanthanum (La) doping (0.2–0.8 at%) on zinc oxide (ZnO) thin films to develop a cost‐effective, efficient, and eco‐friendly room‐temperature CO gas sensor. A low‐cost spray deposition method was used to fabricate pure and La‐doped ZnO thin films to examine their optical, morphological, structural, and CO gas‐sensing characteristics. X‐ray diffraction (XRD) investigation confirmed the formation of a hexagonal wurtzite structure free of secondary phases. Surface morphology analyzed by atomic force microscopy (AFM) revealed a nonmonotonic fluctuation (11.2–44.4) in root‐mean‐square (RMS) roughness with doping concentration, reflecting changes in grain development and refinement. UV–vis spectroscopy showed that films are highly transparent (>80%) across the visible to near‐infrared region. Gas‐sensing results showed that La doping greatly improves sensing performance; 0.6 at% La‐doped film showed the highest response (142%) with fast, repeatable response/recovery behavior (24.4 s/44 s) at room temperature, whereas pure ZnO showed a modest response. These findings highlight the significance of optimal La doping concentration for effective CO gas detection.

Title: Global Solar Energy Trade Network Analysis Using Multilayer Network Approach
Author: Deepti Singh|Ankita Verma
Abstract: Solar energy is a key pillar of the global energy transition, yet some major disruptions in the past show how sensitive its supply chain is to policy shifts and production bottlenecks. In mid-2018 an abrupt change in China's solar subsidy regime created excess photovoltaic inventory and a sharp decline in global module prices, while silicon wafer scarcities during 2021-2022 again reshaped trade flows, underscoring the coupling between upstream materials and downstream manufacturing. Such disruptions propagate through trading relationships between countries rather than through any single market, and network science is the natural framework for studying them: it represents trade as interdependent links, distinguishes suppliers from consumers, identifies systemically important economies, and provides null models against which apparent patterns can be tested rather than assumed. In this paper, we construct a directed Solar Energy Trade Multilayer Network (SETMN) that comprises of three layers corresponding to three products: Polysilicon (HS 280461) and Semi-manufactured silver (HS 710692) and photovoltaic modules (HS 854140). For this purpose, we have utilized UN Comtrade data over the period of 2014-2023. Every metric is referenced to a degree-preserving null model. The network is neither small-world nor scale-free. Clustering lies significantly below its null expectation (z = −8.8 to −3.9), out-degree (α ≈ 1.38) is best described by a truncated power law, the strength distributions are heavy-tailed and best described by a truncated power law or a lognormal, and aggregate in-degree is exponential. Mixing is disassortative (r = −0.33 to −0.29) yet weaker than the degree sequence alone would produce (z = +16.7 to +18.4), which shows that hubs trade with one another more than expected. As a multiplex, the layers share one hub hierarchy (interlayer degree correlation 0.77–0.94) while only 77–92 economies trade in all three stages, so concentration compounds along the supply chain. Export value is held by 5.5–7.4 effective exporters (top five: 66–73%), whereas import absorption is spread across 1.6–3.4 times as many economies, with China leading exports in every year and the United States leading imports from 2019. Trade blocs persist above chance (NMI 0.32–0.46 against a null of 0.07–0.11). The 2018 policy episode leaves almost no imprint on topology and registers at hub level only in United States polysilicon exports (−USD 1.67 bn, p = 0.008; Benjamini–Hochberg q = 0.027 across twelve hub tests, but wild-bootstrap p = 0.094), whereas the 2021 episode produces positive level shifts in all six upstream hub series (p ≤ 0.043), three of which remain significant after false-discovery-rate adjustment (q = 0.027). The apparent post-2021 collapse of the photovoltaic layer is an HS2022 nomenclature artefact rather than a market development. We close with implications for supply-chain resilience.

Title: Flash Flood Mitigation Using a q-Rung Picture Fuzzy Soft EDAS-Based Decision Analytics
Author: Manish Kumar|Tanmay Gupta|Rashid Jan|Taha Radwan
Abstract: Flash floods pose a significant threat to human life, infrastructure, and the environment because of their rapid onset and severe impacts. Developing effective mitigation strategies requires advanced decision-making frameworks capable of addressing uncertainty, vagueness, and complex evaluation criteria. This study proposes a novel multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework that integrates modified q-rung picture fuzzy soft Dombi aggregation operators (q-RPFSf-DAOs) with the Evaluation Based on Distance from Average Solution (EDAS) method. The proposed computational intelligence framework effectively handles imprecise and uncertain information, thereby improving the reliability and flexibility of decision-making processes. The study introduces operational laws, algebraic properties, score and accuracy functions of q-rung picture fuzzy soft numbers, along with advanced aggregation operators under the Dombi environment. Furthermore, the EDAS approach is extended within the proposed fuzzy soft framework to provide a robust and adaptable decision analytics model. A flash flood mitigation decision-support application is conducted to demonstrate the applicability and effectiveness of the proposed methodology in identifying optimal mitigation strategies. Comparative analyses with existing MCDM methods validate the superiority, robustness, and consistency of the proposed framework, highlighting its capability to support reliable decision-making in complex and uncertain environments.

Title: Asymmetric trade gains and development gaps: evaluating the India-Republic of Korea free trade agreement
Author: Sanjay Kumar Mangla|Veena Keshav Pailwar|Vandana Sehgal
Abstract: This study evaluates the structural effectiveness of the India-Republic of Korea free trade agreement (FTA) using bilateral annual trade data from 1995 to 2022. Employing trend analysis, Newey-West and autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) models, we find that while bilateral trade between the two countries is enhanced during the post-FTA period, the trade gains are highly asymmetric, favoring Korea. Trade expansion is driven more by declining trade costs and increasing per capita income of the importing country than by the trade agreement itself. The findings emphasize that FTAs alone are not effective without institutional capacity and export preparedness. From a development perspective, the study indicates that structural asymmetries, regulatory constraints, and underutilization of FTA by small and medium enterprises undermine inclusive trade gains. We argue that emerging economies require sector-specific strategies, institutional reforms, and dynamic policy calibration to ensure that FTAs support inclusive growth, reduce trade imbalances, and align with national development objectives.

Title: Temples and Sustainable Development: Harnessing Sacred Spaces for Environmental Transformation in India
Author: Samdish Sharma|Manas Ranjan Behera
Abstract: The spiritual and cultural centres called temples in India are an important agent to prompt environmental sustainability. With growing emphasis on the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), this paper attempts to explore how sacred sites may support environmental conservation through traditional knowledge, socio-religious influence and economic resources. Through extensive case studies of well-known temples, the book presents best practices achieving sustainable initiatives pertaining to renewable energy integration, water resource management, biodiversity conservation and environmentally friendly waste management. This article also discusses the ways temple economies & governance can influence behavioral change and community level sustainable attainment through faith based education system. In doing so, it is proposed that temples - as both the socio-economic and spiritual foundations for a community - provide India with a ‘golden way’ of approaching the SDGs, that culturally engages communities and transforms India using the same mechanisms of power as before.

Title: Personality traits and attachment styles as predictors of quality of life among young adults: The mediating role of social support- a systematic review
Author: Vanshika Ahuja|Kanupriya Bakhru|Alka Sharma
Abstract: Quality of life (QoL) as a young adult, a person in the grandest decade of your life rests within an immense interplay through individual and interpersonal factors. The current systematic review aimed to analyze the factors that predict QoL as a function of personality traits and attachment styles considering social support as mediator variables. A search of databases Public Med, Scopus, Google Scholar and ResearchGate for articles published in the time window 2018-2025 following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guideline was done. The review synthesised 38 studies that satisfied the inclusion criteria. The results suggested that personality features, especially neuroticism, extraversion and conscientiousness are significant predictors of QoL. Neuroticism was consistently related to negative psychological well-being, whereas extraversion and conscientiousness were positively associated with life satisfaction and adaptive functioning. Attachment styles were also found to be important predictors linked to emotional regulation and relationships with others (i.e. secure attachment versus avoidant/ambivalent/insecure) with the latter predicting psychological distress QoL. Social support that emerged as the main mediating factor in these associations. Higher perceived social support leading to higher quality of life among people with adaptive traits was mediated by secure attachment style. On the other hand, both maladaptive traits and insecure attachment were linked with perceived low support and adverse well-being outcomes. The findings reinforce consideration of intrapersonal characteristics and interpersonal processes in understanding QoL. Nonetheless, some gaps still exist in relation to long-term evidence, diverse cultures, and integrative models. Multidimensional, culturally sensitive approaches that integrate digital support systems are critical for future research. In conclusion, this review highlights that multifaceted interventions may be needed to improve psychosocial aspects of quality of life in young adults and the importance of incorporating them

Title: A p,q,r‑Cubic Quasi‑rung Neutrosophic Fuzzy Decision Model for Enhancing Drone‑Based Logistics
Author: Bhavna Mahant|Rakesh Kumar Bajaj|Vikas Baghel|Tapan Senapati|Hasan Dınçer|Serhat Yüksel
Abstract: Developments in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), or drones, have significantly influenced sectors such as logistics, transportation, surveillance, and emergency response. Selecting the most suitable delivery drone involves evaluating multiple interrelated criteria under uncertainty, including cost-effectiveness, speed, flight range, battery life, payload capacity, and weather adaptability. This study introduces an enhanced p,q,r-CQNFS framework by extending concepts from cubic structures and quasi-rung neutrosophic frameworks. The proposed model integrates these concepts into a unified representation and develops aggregation operators to address uncertainty and imprecision in alternative selection. Furthermore, revised score and accuracy functions are introduced, together with the corresponding operational laws and properties. Weighted and geometric aggregation operators for p,q,r-CQNFSs are employed to develop a methodology for evaluating conflicting criteria in drone selection under complex decision-making scenarios. A numerical example is provided to demonstrate the computational procedure of the proposed methodology. Comparative analyses are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed approach against existing fuzzy and neutrosophic methods. The results illustrate how different representations of uncertain information influence alternative selection and demonstrate the applicability of the proposed framework. Finally, a sensitivity analysis is performed to examine the stability of the alternative rankings under varying parameter values and to identify the strengths and potential limitations of the proposed approach for UAV-based logistics applications.

Title: Nurturing Tomorrow’s Workforce : LGBTQ+ Youth Resilience and Corporate Inclusion in India
Author: Kashish Dua|Kanupriya Misra Bakhru
Abstract: Purpose : This perspective paper developed an upstream human-capital framework linking LGBTQ+ adolescents and young people’s developmental experiences with educational continuity, career development, and future workforce participation in India. Design/Methodology/Approach : A conceptual multidisciplinary approach integrated developmental psychology, LGBTQ+ studies, human-capital economics, strategic human resource management (SHRM), and Indian public policy to develop theoretical pathways rather than estimate effect sizes or establish causality. Findings : The framework proposed that socio-cultural exclusion could create developmental barriers, while supportive environments could strengthen self-efficacy and resilience, potentially supporting educational persistence, career adaptability, and workforce participation. These represented conceptual pathways rather than evidence of direct economic causality. Practical Implications : Policymakers, educational institutions, and corporations could complement workplace diversity, equity, and inclusion through age-appropriate interventions supporting educational continuity, psychosocial well-being, skills development, and career exposure, subject to corporate social responsibility and safeguarding requirements. Originality/Value : The paper extended existing economic arguments for lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender inclusion by shifting attention upstream from workplace inclusion to developmental conditions preceding labor-market entry. It integrated minority stress theory, social cognitive theory, human-capital theory, and SHRM within an Indian LGBTQ+ inclusion framework.

Title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Prediction of Modified Solar Still Productivity Using FGSVM and LOOCV
Author: Pankaj Dumka|Nitesh Pandey|Dhananjay R. Mishra|Rishika Chauhan|Habib Forootan Fard
Abstract: Accurate prediction of freshwater productivity is key to design and optimise solar desalination systems. A Fuzzy Gaussian Support Vector Machine (FGSVM) model is developed in this paper to predict the hourly distillate yield of a sponge-augmented Modified Solar Still (MSS) under real climatic conditions. The experimental data were obtained from the single slope solar still integrated with sponges that enhance evaporation through increase in water retention, capillary action and effective use of thermal energy. Field experiments were conducted at Raghogarh, Guna, India (24°39′N, 77°19′E) using 40 kg of basin water mass. Input parameters were the basin water temperature (Tw), inner glass cover temperature (Tci), solar radiation intensity (I) and the temperature difference between basin water and glass cover (Tw - Tci). The hourly freshwater productivity was used as output variable. To ensure a robust model validation with a limited experimental dataset, training and testing were done using Leave-One-Out Cross Validation (LOOCV). The efficiency of the proposed FGSVM model was evaluated by Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and coefficient of determination (R2). The model gave an RMSE of 14.775, MAE of 11.224 and R2 of 0.980 which indicated an excellent agreement between observed and predicted productivity values. The results show that the FGSVM model can well capture the nonlinear thermal behaviour of the MSS, and the freshwater yield can be predicted accurately. Therefore, the proposed approach can be used as a reliable artificial intelligence tool for productivity forecasting, reducing experimental effort and supporting the development of intelligent and efficient solar desalination systems.

Title: Is the Gain Real? Split Noise, Seed-Only Tests and the Smallest Detectable Gain in Medical Foundation Models
Author: Shreya Bhardwaj|Devanshi Rawat|Ronak Koul
Abstract: Most work on medical foundation models goes into building new ones. Much less goes into checking whether the gains they report are real. A common way to support a claim such as "model A beats model B" is to fine-tune both models a few times with different random seeds on one fixed train/test split, and to run a significance test on the results. This test measures seed noise only, and it can be badly wrong when the split matters. Using 1,372 fine-tuning runs, we show that a five-seed test on one split calls a zero gap significant in a median of 29% of cases, not the planned 5%, and that adding seeds makes it worse. We propose a stricter test that redraws the split for each repeat, and a rule for the smallest gain such a test can detect, about √(AUC(1−AUC)/n) AUROC for n test images. As a worked example we re-test MerMED-FM (The Lancet Digital Health, 2026) on 26 public datasets: of its 28 significant comparisons on public data, 17 hold on new splits, 10 do not survive and 1 reverses. The zip holds every notebook, run score and the scripts that recompute every number without a GPU. This is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

Title: Revamping The Law Of Homicide In India: Legislative Reforms Under The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 And The Pursuit For Global Justice
Author: Mohan Singh Bijalwan|Umesh Kumar
Abstract: In India, for over 160 years, the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC, 1860) was the law for offences of culpable homicide and murder. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), which became effective on 1 July 2024, is a major legislative overhaul of India's substantive criminal law. But how far the BNS has truly changed the law of homicide should be carefully evaluated. As per the study BNS is not a "fundamental" change of homicide law but rather continuity and selective reform. The murder and culpable homicide have retained its fundamental nature of protecting current legal jurisprudence. The BNS makes a number of significant amendments to the way and added certain aggravated types of homicide, especially group killings and killings related to organised criminality or to certain other circumstances. This paper critically examines the legislative changes to homicide under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 specifically in section 100, 101, 103 and 105 vis-à-vis the IPC sections particularly 299, 300, 302 and 304. It reviews how the BNS has tackled some of the thematic issues that have long been raised in connection with the culpable homicide and murder, punishment, mob violence, organised criminality, individual culpability and current methods of unlawful killing. The paper also scrutinises the reforms in the light of constitutional principles of equality, fairness, proportionality and right to life as guaranteed under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution. The paper, concludes that legislative reform needs to be followed by uniformity in interpretation of the law by the Indian judiciary, consistency in practice, procedural safeguards and proportionate sentences, if India's homicide law is to make a meaningful contribution in advancing the larger cause of global justice
